title: I turn 15 years of international sales judgment into tools that people and AI can run together.
subtitle: For decision-makers who want AI to genuinely work inside sales and operations. Background includes mainland China channels (exclusive stores, wholesale, projects) and team management.
services: International sales judgment — payment, delivery, responsibility, and unknowns on one surface, with the decision-maker choosing the next step.
Turning how-to into tools — package one sentence or one judgment into a small tool and process colleagues can use, instead of leaving it in one person's head.
AI without losing control — people learn it first, agents take over step by step; access, approval, and records are clear from the start.

deliverables.title: A clearer decision question
deliverables.body: Objective, constraints, knowns, and unknowns on one surface, so you can see what is stuck.

deliverables.title: Tools the team can pick up
deliverables.body: A sentence or a judgment turned into a small tool or process the team can keep using, with someone responsible for maintaining it.

deliverables.title: A traceable next move
deliverables.body: Evidence to obtain, questions to ask, and the decision that still belongs to the decision-maker.

leverageTitle: HOW I WORK · JUDGMENT FIRST, EXECUTION WITH DISCIPLINE
leverage: AI gives fast direction, organises and drafts; the decision-maker sets the objective and the boundary, and evidence decides what moves forward.
worksTitle: Main works you can open and try
worksLead: Five works, from hands-on play to understanding a flow, to business judgment and practical AI.
works: ROOMVERSE 3D — turn a 3D living room, change the walls and the light; in “Feeling First”, see how a person deepens a prepared AI draft into details you can live with.
Trade Street — an interactive way to see how one container gets to sea, even for non-specialists.
Which Step Holds? — order an enterprise AI rollout for a fictional company.
Commercial Decision Desk — before any commitment, net contribution, payment, and unknowns on one table; the decision-maker decides.
AI Lab — seventeen chapters of practical AI, from individuals to enterprises, with interactive tools such as “How Many Agents?”
process: Bring one product, an old catalogue, a stuck process, or a task you want AI to help with. Clarify where it is stuck first, then decide the next step.
disclaimer: Demo cases use fictional data; outcomes not verified.
